name: Box cutter
description: A plastic box cutter with a snap-off blade that slides out of its nose. Opens cartons and cuts cloth, but makes a poor weapon.
notes: The reference's butchering 8 is left out: the blade is too short to dress a carcass. Box and volume x1.51 come from the slider and grip pad standing proud of the body.

name: Copper knife
description: A leaf-shaped blade hammered from copper on a round copper grip. Soft and quick to dull, but it cuts.
notes: A crafted item, so it has no loot economy. butchering is a new quality name; the levels are a first guess against the stone knife and pocket knife. The raised centre rib is drawn in bronze so the hammered ridge shows against the copper.

name: Uncapping knife
description: A beekeeper's knife with a long, flat, double-edged blade for slicing the wax caps off honeycomb. Clumsy, but it will cut.
notes: The reference lists steel only; the handle is drawn in wood with a brass ferrule, as uncapping knives are made. Box and volume x2.69 come from the bounding box of a flat 45 mm blade; the solid volume is close to the reference. A melee profile can follow the kitchen knife's when the drafts are applied.

name: Pocket knife
description: A small folding knife with red plastic scales and a single clip-point blade. Fits in any pocket and is sharp enough for most small jobs.
notes: Drawn opened so it reads as a knife; the reference's 10 ml is the closed knife, hence box and volume x2.34. The reference gives no longest side; 115 mm open is a typical small pocket knife. Deadvox has no folded state, so a closed model would need its own state.

name: Stone knife
description: A knapped stone blade set into a split wooden handle and bound with hide. Crude, but it holds an edge.
notes: A crafted item, so it has no loot economy. The hide lashing is drawn in skin-rawhide; the reference names only wood and stone. Lighter flake scars on the blade mark it as knapped.

name: Stone chopper
description: A fist-sized river stone with flakes knocked off one side to leave a rough cutting edge. The crudest blade there is.
notes: A crafted item, so it has no loot economy. The reference's negative butchering rating, which marks it as worse than bare hands for dressing a carcass, is left out rather than given a level. The fresh flaked edge is drawn lighter than the weathered cortex.

name: Bill
description: A hooked steel blade with a back spur, socketed onto a long wooden shaft. Made for clearing hedges and brush; just as good at keeping something at arm's length.
notes: The reference describes it as looking like a glaive; it is drawn as a hedging bill, a shorter hooked blade on a long shaft, which suits a landscaping tool. chopping and grass_cutting are new quality names. Box and volume x2.30 come from the bounding box of a long shaft; the solid volume is close to the reference. The size is a guess for a 1.5 m polearm. A two-handed melee profile can follow when the drafts are applied.

name: Bronze bill
description: A hooked bronze blade with a back spur, socketed onto a long wooden shaft. Heavier than steel and softer at the edge.
notes: Rides on the bill's model with a bronze head. Mass 3.0 kg from the reference, against the steel bill's 2.4 kg. A crafted item, so it has no loot economy.

name: Digging stick
description: A stout stick with one end carved into a flat blade and hardened in the fire. Loosens soil for shallow holes, but no more.
notes: A crafted item, so it has no loot economy. digging is a new quality name. The blackened tip shows the fire hardening; a bark knot partway up marks it as a cut branch.
